newsitem.title: BOSNIA: World Bank details Bosnia reconstruction aid.
newsitem.headline: World Bank details Bosnia reconstruction aid.

text.p: The World Bank said on Thursday almost $600 million had been given out for reconstruction projects in war-shattered Bosnia, but virtually none of it in the semi-autonomous Serb Republic.
Rory O'Sullivan, the bank's representative in Bosnia, said that of $1.9 billion pledged, $558 million had been disbursed, and $880 million was now committed.
"This is a substantial amount, we expect this amount will increase," he told reporters, adding that August and September had seen large increases in commitments.
O'Sullivan said the improvement was due to increasing stability in Bosnia after the Dayton peace accords.
"If we don't have political stability, it is impossible to have a sensible programme implemented," he said.

He said post-war reconstruction projects were now going very well but added that a "major catching-up effort" was required in the Serb Republic (Republika Srpska -- RS) which had received only 1.5 percent of the $558 million.
The Serb Republic, which wants to deal directly with international institutions, has refused to accept money channelled through the Bosnian government.

"Donor activity in Republika Srpska has reached only a small fraction of that in the federation," said a joint statement released by the World Bank and the European Union. "A major donor effort will be required to enable the RS to catch up."
O'Sullivan said the World Bank had five projects, ranging from education to engineering. He hoped Saturday's elections in Bosnia would clear the way towards implementing them.
He said the Dayton accords were clear on the need to create a central bank and single currency and he believed this would soon be done.
"The parties have been cooperating closely on this," he said.
